note: Names, descriptions and grades are exactly as PlayStation publishes them. Guides are written for this entry in our own words. Where a method is not confirmed in-game yet, the guide says so plainly.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (43531)

trophies.guide: The platinum pops automatically once the other 54 trophies are earned. There is no separate task: follow this guide's roadmap in order — story first, then contacts and strangers, then activities, then collectibles, and finally the 100% cleanup — and the platinum is the last thing you hear. Keep this tracker open as you play so nothing is left to guess at the end.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing. It is the first story mission, so just play through the opening: follow the on-screen prompts, learn the basic movement, driving and interaction controls, and see the mission through to its end card. Unmissable in a normal playthrough — it pops when the mission completes. Method confirmed by the official description alone; no outside walkthrough needed.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Play through every story mission in Chapter 1 until the chapter closes. Do the missions in the order the game offers them and do not rush past side content the chapter introduces, since later chapters build on it. The trophy pops at the chapter's end card. Tied to a single story moment, so it is flagged missable here, but it cannot be skipped by playing the story normally.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Play through every story mission in Chapter 2 until the chapter closes. Keep an eye on the mission list as you go: chapter trophies only count story missions, so optional activities do not advance them. The trophy pops at the end card of the chapter's final mission.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Play through every story mission in Chapter 3 until the chapter closes. By this point the map is opening up, so it is worth doing the activities and stranger missions that appear along the way — they feed the activity and stranger trophies later — but the chapter trophy itself only needs the story missions done.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Play through every story mission in Chapter 4 until the chapter closes. This is the last numbered chapter, so finish any chapter-specific side content you still want before moving on to the finale — once the story moves past a chapter, its moment is gone. The trophy pops at the chapter's end card.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission. There is only one finale, so play the story to its end and complete the last mission when it is offered. The gold pops on the end card. Before you start it, consider saving first and finishing any remaining story-tied side content — after the finale the game continues in free roam, but a first-run story moment cannot be replayed except through mission replay, if the game offers it.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run when it appears in the mission list. Play it through to its end card. It is a named story mission, so it only pops from that mission — free-roam play does not count. If you are unsure whether you have done it, check the mission log: a completed Breakfast Run is the proof.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions in GTA games usually have a setup phase first, so do the setups the game offers and then run the heist itself to its end card. The trophy pops when the heist mission completes, not when a setup does.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play when it appears. Play it to its end card. Named story missions like this one are the only way to earn the trophy, so do not leave it sitting in the mission list while you wander off into free roam for hours — finish it when it comes up.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. This is a named story mission, so the trophy pops only from finishing that mission to its end card. Keep your health and supplies topped up before starting it, as with any story mission, and play it through in one go where you can.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown. VCIA is Vice City International Airport, so expect this mission to involve the airport area. Finish the mission to its end card and the trophy pops. As a named story mission it cannot be earned any other way.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The name suggests a large set-piece mission, so go in prepared and follow the mission objectives rather than improvising. The trophy pops at the mission's end card.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's stats screen. In GTA games this means finishing the story, all stranger missions, all collectibles, all activities and all the checklist items the game counts — it is the last gold most players earn, just before the platinum. Do not chase it first: play the roadmap in order, tick off the other trophies, and use the in-game completion percentage to find what is left. The exact checklist is whatever the game's stats screen shows; no outside list replaces it.
trophies.name: A Long Road
sources: PowerPyx — GTA 6 Trophy Guide (method not yet confirmed in-game)

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, long air time and similar driving feats. The counter is cumulative across the whole playthrough, so every stunt you do while travelling counts; you do not need 250 in one session. The fastest route is to use stunt jumps and fast cars on long straight roads, and to keep doing small stunts whenever you drive instead of only in dedicated sessions. Count: 250, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity at least once — fishing, races, shooting range, drone races, arcade games, bowling, meditation, hunting and the other activities the game lists. You only need one attempt at each, not a win. Work through the activity list early: open each one, try it, and tick it off here. Count: 9 activity types, per the official list's companion data.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Go to a shooting range, pick a challenge, and beat its gold score or time. Work through them one weapon or drill at a time, and repeat any challenge you miss — they are all repeatable, so a bad run costs nothing but time. Use the weapon the challenge gives you, aim for the gold threshold shown before you start, and learn each drill's pattern instead of rushing. Count: 42 challenges, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Find each race location, learn its course with a practice run if the game allows it, then race to win — only wins count, and you need one at every location. Drone races reward smooth lines over raw speed, so cut corners where the course allows and avoid crashing, which costs more time than a cautious line. Count: 14 locations, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Each race only counts once, so you need 20 distinct race events, not 20 wins of the same one. Work through the race list across Leonida, using a fast car suited to each race's surface, and tick each win off here. Races are repeatable, so a loss just means trying again.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Find Cal and take his fishing challenge, then out-fish him: watch the bite cues, keep the tension right so the line does not snap, and land the bigger catch. If you lose, challenge him again — fishing challenges are repeatable. Specific spot and bait details are not confirmed in-game yet; the method above follows from the official description.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
sources: PlayStationTrophies.org — GTA 6 Trophy Guide (method not yet confirmed in-game)

trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game from start to its end screen. Find an arcade machine, pick a game, and play it through — you do not need a high score, just a completed game. Any arcade game counts, so pick the shortest one you enjoy. If you fail, start again; arcade games are repeatable.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's last mission. Contact missions unlock as you meet and work for each contact, so play Andy's strand through in order until his final mission appears, then complete it to its end card. Contact strands are easy to leave half-done while chasing the story, so clear them before the finale where you can.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's last mission. Work through Kenton's missions in order until his final one is offered, then complete it. As with the other contacts, do his strand when it appears rather than leaving it for after the story — the final mission is the payoff for the whole strand.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's last mission. Play Billy's mission strand through in order until the final mission appears, then complete it to its end card. Tick Billy off in the roadmap's contact stage so no contact strand is forgotten at the end.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida. Strangers appear as markers on the map — meet them, do their missions, and follow each strand to its end. You need 8 complete strands, not 8 single missions, so keep returning to a stranger until their story is done. Explore the whole map: strangers are spread across the state, not just in Vice City. Count: 8 strands, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's last mission. Work through Randy's strand in order until his final mission is offered, then complete it. Contact final missions are the natural end of each strand, so if Randy's strand stalls, check the map for his marker — you may simply not have met him yet.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's last mission. Play Tyrone's strand through in order until his final mission appears, then complete it to its end card. Five contacts have final-mission trophies — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone — so clearing all five strands is one clean stage of the roadmap.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. Find each spot — usually a quiet viewpoint — and use the meditate prompt there. Spots are spread across the whole map, so combine this with the exploration trophy: meditate whenever you reach a new area. Keep a checklist here; the count is 18, per PSNProfiles, and the exact spots are not confirmed in-game yet.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Talk to Bret to learn which animal he wants and where it roams, then track it — move quietly, watch for its signs, and take the shot cleanly. Only the unique animal counts, not ordinary hunting. The animal's exact location is not confirmed in-game yet; follow Bret's directions in-game rather than any outside map.
trophies.name: Fair Game
sources: PlayStationTrophies.org — GTA 6 Trophy Guide (method not yet confirmed in-game)

trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida — pick them up as you explore, and check which set each card belongs to so you can see which sets are close to complete. You need 3 finished sets, not every card in the game, so focus on the sets you are nearest to completing first. Card locations are not confirmed in-game yet; collect as you explore and use this tracker to count sets, not single cards.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK feature at 100 different locations. WAiNK is the in-game way to mark or interact with a spot, so do it whenever you arrive somewhere new — the counter is cumulative and each location only counts once. Spread it across the whole playthrough: 100 locations is a long grind if left to the end, and a quick habit if done as you travel. Count: 100 locations, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's small objectives — driving, shooting, exploration and more — and they stack up naturally as you play. Check the challenge list in-game, pick off the easy ones first, and let the rest come while you work on other trophies. You need 50 completed, not 50 of one kind. Count: 50, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose it and escape. Get the cops to 4 stars — committing crimes in a busy area does it — then break line of sight, hide until the wanted level drops, and get clear with your partner still with you. Keep a fast car ready before you start, and do not let your partner get left behind in the chase.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, keeping your wanted level the whole time. Plan a route with 3 shops close together, rob the first, move straight to the next, and keep going — do not lose the cops between robberies, or the chain breaks. A fast getaway car parked nearby helps, and doing it in a quieter part of town keeps the wanted level manageable. If the chain breaks, start over; it is repeatable.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Every new vehicle you drive or encounter counts, so drive everything you see — parked cars, bikes, boats, aircraft — instead of sticking to one favourite. The counter is cumulative, so it grows naturally if you vary your rides; if it stalls late on, hunt for rare vehicle types you have not driven yet. Count: 100 vehicles, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Down 5 enemies during one single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-aim ability, so trigger it in a fight with at least 5 enemies close together, then take them down one by one before it runs out. Pick a busy firefight — story missions with groups of enemies are ideal — and do not waste the ability on a single straggler. If you only get 4, try again; it is repeatable. Count: 5 in one use, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave Vice City International Airport in an unscheduled way — that is, take an aircraft and go, without a ticket or a plan. Get to VCIA, find a plane, get in and take off. Expect attention from airport security, so be ready to fly away fast once you are airborne. The exact trigger is not confirmed in-game yet; the method follows from the official description.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
sources: PlayStationTrophies.org — GTA 6 Trophy Guide (method not yet confirmed in-game)

trophies.guide: Deal with the Rhinos — the military tanks. The description is deliberately vague, as a hidden trophy's is: expect this to involve a Rhino tank, whether driving one, surviving one, or taking one on. Keep an eye out for tanks around military areas and missions, and try interacting with one when you find it. The precise trigger is not confirmed in-game yet, so this guide does not invent one.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being seen. Plan it like a stealth job: go in quiet, avoid the cameras and guards' line of sight, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails — leave, let things calm down, and try again. Night and a quiet approach help; a loud entrance does not.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time. Find the banks, break into their vaults, take the money and get away clean — the escape counts, so a robbery that ends in a bust does not. Plan your getaway before you go in, and do the vaults one at a time across the playthrough rather than all at once. Vault locations are not confirmed in-game yet. Count: 5 vaults, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Find a truck on its route, stop it — ramming it or blocking the road works in GTA games — take the money and get away before the police close in. Have a fast getaway vehicle ready and a route out of the area planned before you strike. If the escape fails, try another truck; they run regularly.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. Travel the whole map — every named area counts when you enter it. Drive, fly and sail to the corners of the state, not just Vice City: the countryside, the keys, the swamps and the small towns all hold areas. Use this alongside the meditation and WAiNK trophies, which also reward covering the map. Count: 52 areas, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Find the gangs' operations around Leonida, hit one per gang, and get away. You need one per gang, not nine total from the same gang, so keep a list of which gangs you have done. Operations are usually guarded, so go in ready. Count: 9 gangs, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach, find a bar or vendor with a view of the ocean, and enjoy a cocktail there. The trophy is about the moment, not a challenge: sit, order the drink, and let it count. Do it during a relaxed trip to the beach — it pairs well with the exploration trophy, since Ocean Beach is one of the areas to visit anyway.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a vehicle straight through a showroom's windows and out the other side, in classic GTA style. Pick a showroom with a car inside, get in, and floor it through the glass. It is a one-off stunt, so save first if you want a clean run, and expect a wanted level on the way out — have an escape in mind.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
sources: PlayStationTrophies.org — GTA 6 Trophy Guide (method not yet confirmed in-game)

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Bowl at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and follow through — that is, complete a game there. Go to the alley, start a game of bowling, and play it to the end. Any score counts; finishing the game is what matters. It pairs with the activity trophy, since bowling is one of the activity types to try.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: Reach a partnership moment with mass appeal — the description is vague on purpose, as a hidden trophy's is. It relates to the partnership between the two leads, so expect it to pop from a story or side moment where the partnership wins the crowd over. Play the story and the partner activities, and it should come naturally; the precise trigger is not confirmed in-game yet, so this guide does not invent one.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Make choices — 500 of them, per PSN's counter. Choices happen all through the game: dialogue picks, mission decisions, how you treat people, what you buy and how you play. You cannot grind this one in a single sitting; it accumulates across the whole playthrough, so just keep playing and making decisions. It is flagged missable here because choices, once made, cannot be unmade — but 500 is a large count, so a normal full playthrough should reach it. Count: 500, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Succeed on your second try at something — fail once, then get it right the second time. The description is vague on purpose: the natural reading is to fail a mission or challenge, then pass it on the immediate retry. If you fail anything during normal play, take the retry seriously instead of reloading an old save, and the trophy should pop when you succeed. The precise trigger is not confirmed in-game yet.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — a random event, an odd encounter, or something that makes you stop and stare. Leonida is full of strange sights, so keep exploring, especially off the beaten track and at odd hours. You cannot force a random event, so treat this as a trophy that finds you while you play rather than one to hunt. The precise trigger is not confirmed in-game yet, so this guide does not invent one.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by — that is, hit someone with a melee weapon while driving past. Get a melee weapon, find a target on foot, and drive by close enough to land the hit without stopping. It is a timing trick: slow down just enough to connect, then keep driving. If you miss, circle back and try again; it is repeatable.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from certain robberies and jobs; they are not clean cash until a contact launders them for you, for a cut. Keep laundering what you earn instead of spending it dirty, and the total climbs across the playthrough. Bank vaults and armored trucks are good sources of marked money. Count: $250,000, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops in total. Buy weapons, clothes, cars, food and anything else — the counter adds up everything you spend in shops across the whole game. It comes naturally if you buy gear as you go; if it is the last one standing, buy an expensive car or weapon to close the gap. Count: $100,000, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties. Garages are properties you can purchase around Leonida; each one gives you somewhere to store vehicles. You need all 8, so save up and buy them as they become available — property purchases are also a good way to spend toward the $100,000 trophy. Count: 8 garages, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles in the Scooter Bros app. Find vehicles, then register each one through the app — each registration counts once, so you need 10 different vehicles. Combine this with the 100-vehicle discovery trophy: register vehicles as you discover them instead of leaving it all to the end. Count: 10 vehicles, per PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: On the Spot
